go:500.title: GATE CSE 1991 | Question: 01-iii
go:500.question:
Consider the number given by the decimal expression:
$$16^3*9 + 16^2*7 + 16*5+3$$
The number of $1’s$ in the unsigned binary representation of the number is ______

go:516.title: GATE CSE 1991 | Question: 03-ii
go:516.question:
Advantage of synchronous sequential circuits over asynchronous ones is:

  1. faster operation
  2. ease of avoiding problems due to hazards
  3. lower hardware requirement
  4. better noise immunity
  5. none of the above

go:523.title: GATE CSE 1991 | Question: 03-viii
go:523.question:
Consider the following Pascal function:

Function X(M:integer):integer;
Var i:integer;
Begin
    i := 0;
    while i*i < M
    do i:= i+1
    X := i
 end

The function call $X(N)$, if $N$ is positive, will return

  1. $\lfloor\sqrt N \rfloor$
  2. $\lfloor\sqrt N \rfloor +1$
  3. $\lceil \sqrt N \rceil$
  4. $\lceil \sqrt N \rceil +1$
  5. None of the above

go:524.title: GATE CSE 1991 | Question: 03,x
go:524.question:
Indicate all the true statements from the following:

  1. Recursive descent parsing cannot be used for grammar with left recursion.
  2. The intermediate form for representing expressions which is best suited for code optimization is the postfix form.
  3. A programming language not supporting either recursion or pointer type does not need the support of dynamic memory allocation.
  4. Although C does not support call-by-name parameter passing, the effect can be correctly simulated in C
  5. No feature of Pascal typing violates strong typing in Pascal.

go:26442.title: GATE CSE 1991 | Question: 5-c
go:26442.question: Find the maximum clock frequency at which the counter in the figure below can be operated. Assume that the propagation delay through each flip flop and each AND gate is $10\;\text{ns}$. Also, assume that the setup time for the $JK$ inputs of the flip flops is negligible.

go:540.title: GATE CSE 1991 | Question: 13
go:540.question: Give an optimal algorithm in pseudo-code for sorting a sequence of $n$ numbers which has only $k$ distinct numbers ($k$ is not known a Priori). Give a brief analysis for the time-complexity of your algorithm.

go:515.title: GATE CSE 1991 | Question: 03.i
go:515.question:
Choose the correct alternatives (more than one may be correct) and write the corresponding letters only:

The advantages of CMOS technology over a MOS is:

  1. lower power dissipation

  2. greater speed

  3. smaller chip size

  4. fewer masks for fabrication

go:517.title: GATE CSE 1991 | Question: 03.iii
go:517.question:
Choose the correct alternatives (more than one may be correct) and write the corresponding letters only:

The total size of address space in a virtual memory system is limited by:

  1. the length of MAR

  2. the available secondary storage

  3. the available main memory

  4. all of the above

go:518.title: GATE CSE 1991 | Question: 03.iv
go:518.question:
Choose the correct alternatives (more than one may be correct) and write the corresponding letters only:

The TRAP interrupts mechanism of the 8085 microprocessor:

  1. executes an RST by hardware

  2. executes an instruction supplied by an external device through the INTA signal

  3. executes an instruction from memory location 20H

  4. executes a NOP

go:519.title: GATE CSE 1991 | Question: 03.ix
go:519.question:
Choose the correct alternatives (more than one may be correct ) and write the corresponding letters only

A "link editor" is a program that:

  1. matches the parameters of the macro-definition with locations of the parameters of the macro call

  2. matches external names of one program with their location in other programs

  3. matches the parameters of subroutine definition with the location of parameters of subroutine call.

  4. acts as a link between text editor and the user

go:520.title: GATE CSE 1991 | Question: 03.v
go:520.question:
Choose the correct alternatives (more than one may be correct) and write the corresponding letters only:

The ALE line of an 8085 microprocessor is used to:

  1. Latch the output of an I/O instruction into an external latch.

  2. Deactivate the chip-select signal from memory devices.

  3. Latch the 8 bits of address lines AD7-AD0 into an external latch.

  4. Find the interrupt enable status of the TRAP interrupt.

go:521.title: GATE CSE 1991 | Question: 03.vi
go:521.question:
Choose the correct alternatives (more than one may be correct) and write the corresponding letters only:

Kruskal's algorithm for finding a minimum spanning tree of a weighted graph G with n vertices and m edges has the time complexity of:

  1. [latex]O(n^{2})[/latex]

  2. O(mn)

  3. O(m+n)

  4. [latex]O(m \log n)[/latex]

go:522.title: GATE CSE 1991 | Question: 03.vii
go:522.question:
Choose the correct alternatives (more than one may be correct) and write the corresponding letters only:

The following sequence of operations is performed on a stack:

PUSH (10), PUSH (20), POP, PUSH (10), PUSH (20), POP, POP, POP, PUSH (20), POP

The sequence of values popped out is

  1. 20,10,20,10,20

  2. 20,20,10,10,20

  3. 10,20,20,10,20

  4. 20,20,10,20,10

go:528.title: GATE CSE 1991 | Question: 03.xiv
go:528.question:
Choose the correct alternatives (more than one may be correct) and write the corresponding letters only:

Which of the following is the strongest correct statement about a finite language over some finite alphabet [latex]\Sigma[/latex]?

  1. It could be undecidable

  2. It is Turing-machine recognizable

  3. It is a context sensitive language.

  4. It is a regular language.

go:525.title: GATE CSE 1991 | Question: 03.xi
go:525.question:
Choose the correct alternatives (more than one can be correct) and write the corresponding letters only:

Indicate all the false statements from the statements given below:

  1. The amount of virtual memory available is limited by the availability of the secondary memory

  2. Any implementation of a critical section requires the use of an indivisible machine- instruction ,such as test-and-set.

  3. The use of monitors ensure that no dead-locks will be caused .

  4. The LRU page-replacement policy may cause thrashing for some type of programs.

go:526.title: GATE CSE 1991 | Question: 03.xii
go:526.question:
Choose the correct alternatives (more than one may be correct) and write the corresponding letters only:

If [latex]F_1[/latex], [latex]F_2[/latex] and [latex]F_3[/latex] are propositional formulae such that [latex]F_1 \land F_2 \rightarrow F_3[/latex] and [latex]F_1 \land F_2 \rightarrow \sim F_3[/latex] are both tautologies, then which of the following is true:

  1. Both[latex]F_1[/latex] and [latex]F_2[/latex] are tautologies

  2. The conjunction [latex]F_1 \land F_2[/latex] is not satisfiable

  3. Neither is tautologous

  4. Neither is satisfiable

go:527.title: GATE CSE 1991 | Question: 03.xiii
go:527.question:
Choose the correct alternatives (more than one may be correct) and write the corresponding letters only.

Let [latex]r=1(1+0)^*, s=11^*0 \text{ and } t=1^*0[/latex] be three regular expressions. Which one of the following is true?

  1. [latex]L(s) \subseteq L(r) \text{ and } L(s) \subseteq L(t)[/latex]

  2. [latex]L(r) \subseteq L(s) \text{ and } L(s) \subseteq L(t)[/latex]

  3. [latex]L(s) \subseteq L(t) \text{ and } L(s) \subseteq L(r)[/latex]

  4. [latex]L(t) \subseteq L(s)\text{ and } L(s) \subseteq L(r)[/latex]
